items: Я пойду в школу завтра, если я буду здоров.
I'll go to school tomorrow if I am well.
Он работает в библиотеке, если библиотека открыта сегодня.
He is working in the library if the library is open today.

blocks.text: A sentence involving such a clause states that an event will take place if the condition is fulfilled. Being statements of direct fact, they are expressed by the indicative mood.
The future condition is expressed in English by the present tense, whereas in Russian it is expressed by the future.

items.text: In sentences of this type the conditions postulated by the «**если бы**» clause are either improbable or downright contrary to existing fact. *Если бы я был здоров, я пошёл бы в школу.* —
points: If I were well, I would go to school tomorrow.

If I had been well, I would have gone to school yesterday. The English language uses special forms of the verb for each of these two types of supposition, whereas the Russian language, making no grammatical distinction between them, uses one form which may express either type, depending on the context.
Main clause: past tense of the verb with the particle «**бы**» following the predicate, or (rarely) the subject.
Subordinate clause: begins with «**если бы (б)**», the verb being in the past tense. *Если бы он знал это, он завтра же поехал бы туда.*

blocks.text: Caution: Not every English construction with "would" expresses the conditional mood. "Would" may also denote the "future-in-the-past".
The Russian equivalent for such constructions is the future tense: *Он сказал, что он придёт позже.* — He said he would come later.

items: Я пошёл бы в кино, но у меня нет времени.
Он помог бы вам, но вы его не позвали.
Если бы не вы, мы всё ещё искали бы квартиру.
But for you we would still be looking for an apartment.
Посидели бы у нас ещё немного!
Я хотел бы попросить вашего совета.
I would like to ask your advice.
Oh, that Friday would come soon!

blocks.text: The English "if", equivalent of "whether", has the Russian equivalent **ЛИ**. The particle **ЛИ** never begins the clause; it takes the second place following the word to which the question or doubt refers: *Спроси его, говорит ли он по-немецки. Я не знаю, сделают ли они это.* But: *Мы дадим ему работу, если он говорит по-немецки.*

items: Я бы пошёл в кино́, **е́сли** бы у меня́ бы́ло вре́мя.
I would have gone to the cinema if I had had time.
once, one day, once upon a time

exercises.q: Модуль называется полупростым, ___ (if) он разлагается в прямую сумму простых подмодулей.
exercises.prompt: A module is said to be semisimple if it is the sum of simple submodules.

exercises.q: Все экономические проблемы бы решились, ___ (if (unreal)) самоудовлетворённость обложили налогом.
exercises.prompt: All economic problems would be solved, if they made complacency taxable.
exercises.why: **если бы** — «if» in an unreal condition (improbable or contrary to fact): если бы, with the verb in the past tense.

exercises.q: ___ (if) ты в Париже, можешь посетить Лувр.
exercises.prompt: If you are in Paris, you can visit the Louvre.

exercises.q: Не верь статистике, ___ (if) только сам её не подделывал.
exercises.prompt: Don't trust statistics that you haven't falsified yourself.

exercises.q: ___ (if (unreal)) да кабы, то во рту росли б грибы.
exercises.prompt: If mice flew, they would look like birds.
exercises.why: **Если бы** — «if» in an unreal condition (improbable or contrary to fact): если бы, with the verb in the past tense.

exercises.q: Было бы обидно, ___ (if (unreal)) ты этого не сделал.
exercises.prompt: It would be disappointing if you didn't do that.
exercises.why: **если бы** — «if» in an unreal condition (improbable or contrary to fact): если бы, with the verb in the past tense.
